what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a septic replacement at 290 New West Townsend Road with standard conditions, by unanimous roll call.
It approved the 451 Townsend Harbor Road house filing, with one member recused, and approved homes on Lots 3 and 4 Holman Street unanimously.
Three hearings, at 408 Electric Ave, 509 Townsend Harbor Road and 127 Chase Road, were continued to October 5 for missing plan details or a DEP file number.
The commission accepted the encroachment fix at 100 Woodland Drive and approved a purchase order for pollinator-habitat fencing to protect new trees from deer.
It appointed Richard Tremblay to the stormwater committee, and put off the election of officers because not all members were present.

why_it_matters: Wetlands approvals set the conditions for septic systems and new homes near protected resources, and an applicant whose plan is incomplete waits a full meeting cycle for a decision.
The fencing purchase is a small town expense, chosen from three quotes, that shows how the commission spends on habitat work.
watch_next: The October 5 meeting, when the 408 Electric Ave, 509 Townsend Harbor Road and 127 Chase Road hearings resume.
The future meeting where the commission is to hold its election of officers.

Volunteers asked for a used water tank, cinder blocks and deer fencing; the tank and blocks were approved from petty cash, and fencing needs vendor quotes.
The agent reported the fund balance as enough to cover the maintenance and purchases.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued most wetlands hearings, including 137 Chase Road and the Fitchburg Land Owner LLC hearing, and held several for missing DEP file numbers.
It issued negative determinations for the 4 Kimball Street sewer extension and for 362 Townsend Harbor Road, and approved 37 Spring Street with a standard order of conditions.
The commission voted to have applicants pay newspapers directly for hearing ads, because those fees go to the general fund rather than the conservation budget.
It approved a Smart Sign trail-sign purchase order from the timber rights fund, an annual exterminator contract, and a used water tank and cinder blocks for the pollinator habitat.
The Sunny Hill Road Chapter 61B right of first refusal was left on the agenda for a later meeting, and election of officers was deferred until all members can participate.

why_it_matters: Fees for hearing ads now go from applicants straight to newspapers instead of into the general fund, so the conservation budget no longer handles them.
Budgets for the Hollis Road and timber rights revolving funds were not yet set, so bills could not yet be paid from them.
The town's right of first refusal on the Sunny Hill Road parcel is still undecided, and the minutes record no funds currently available to buy land.
watch_next: Continued hearings return September 21, including 137 Chase Road and 507 Townsend Harbor Road; the Fitchburg Land Owner LLC hearing is set for October 5.
The Sunny Hill Road 61B right of first refusal returns to a future agenda so absent members can weigh in.
